reuse.why: Builds on the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend/getDayWithSkippedWeekend/getNextDate and adds shared predicates (skipsWeekendOccurrences, isNonWorkingDay, getDailyTakeCount) that every consumer imports rather than re-deriving the daily rule.

duplication.why: The daily and holiday predicates are shared, but the per-occurrence 'drop if daily, else move' dispatch is still written separately in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange.

placement.why: Date rules live in shared/schedules.ts, the handler in schedules/app.ts and config typing in types/models, matching the tree's layering.

scope.why: Changes are limited to the four requested steps plus tests; parseRecurDate carrying frequency/holidays is required by them.

maintainability.why: Named predicates and documented bounds make the rule easy to follow, though the inverted noSkipWeekend argument in schedule-template and the repeated drop/move dispatch add friction.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All consumers use the shared skipsWeekendOccurrences, isNonWorkingDay and getDateWithSkippedWeekend; none re-implements them

disguised_duplication.where: getUpcomingDates (filter/slice vs map) and getDatesInRange (loop with continue and ternary) reshape the same drop-or-move occurrence dispatch instead of sharing one adjust-occurrence function

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend and getDayWithSkippedWeekend each gain a holidays parameter; getNextDate gains a daily drop branch; getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange each decide drop-vs-move themselves around the shared helpers
